corridors.name: The Eifel road - Nattenheim to the Taunus
notes: Out of the Eifel over the Büchel TACAN and the Rhine at Koblenz to the Taunus VORTAC - clear of the Nike sites of 6/56 ADA (Spangdahlem / Bitburg / Hahn) and 2/62 ADA's HAWK batteries round Bitburg (Balesfeld, Butzweiler, Hisel).

corridors.name: Recovery into the Eifel
notes: Back down the Eifel road. SOC 3 Kindsbach (4 ATAF); CRC Börfink 'SCANDALISE'.

corridors.name: The Hunsrück road - Hahn to the Taunus
notes: Hahn, Pferdsfeld and Büchel east over the Hunsrück to the Kirn VORTAC and the Taunus - the 94th Group's Nike sites at Dichtelbach and Wüschheim below.
corridors.src: OurAirports HND/KIR/TAU; en.wikipedia List of Nike missile sites

corridors.name: Recovery over the Hunsrück
notes: Kirn back to the Hahn DME.

corridors.name: The Kirn road - Ramstein to the Taunus
notes: Ramstein and Zweibrücken north over the Kirn VORTAC to the Taunus, between the Nike sites of 2/60 ADA (Ramstein / Pirmasens / Kaiserslautern) and the 94th Group's Hunsrück sites (Dichtelbach, Wüschheim).

corridors.name: Recovery via Kirn
notes: The Kirn road back into the Pfalz; Ramstein TACAN 113.4.

corridors.name: Rhein-Main to the Taunus
notes: Wiesbaden and Frankfurt out over the Taunus VORTAC to Gelnhausen, under the 10th ADA Group's HAWK (Hanau, Giessen) - SOC 3 Kindsbach's identification zone.

corridors.name: Recovery into Rhein-Main
notes: Gelnhausen to the Taunus VORTAC and down into Wiesbaden / Rhein-Main.

corridors.name: The Fulda Gap - LLTR to Point Alpha
notes: The V US Corps road: Gelnhausen, Fulda, Hünfeld, through the HAWK belt (2/2 ADA Giessen, 1/1 ADA Wildflecken) to the gate at OP Alpha. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.

corridors.name: The Werra road - LLTR to Herleshausen
notes: North of the Fulda Gap: the Vogelsberg to Alsfeld and the A4 crossing at Wartha / Herleshausen - the III GE Corps sector, FlaRakGrp 38's HAWK (Freienhagen, Flechtdorf, Rhoden) to the north. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.

corridors.name: The Harz road - Kassel to Helmstedt
notes: 4 ATAF's road to the North German Plain: the Fritzlar NDB, the Warburg VOR over the ATAF seam at Kassel, Goslar under the Harz, and the Helmstedt gate. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.

corridors.name: The Hof corridor - Würzburg to Hof
notes: The VII US Corps road: Würzburg (69th ADA Group HQ), Bayreuth in the ADIZ, and the Hof gate - the Zwickau axis in reverse. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.

corridors.name: The Ruhr road - Cologne to the Porta
notes: Nörvenich and Cologne east over the Cola and Germinghausen VORs to Hamm, Gütersloh and the Minden Gap at Porta Westfalica - NORTHAG's 'vital ground'. CRC Uedem 'CRABTREE', CRC Erndtebrück 'LONESHIP'.
corridors.src: OurAirports COL/GMH/HMM; JMSS (Minden Gap); relikte.com CRC call signs

corridors.name: Recovery into the Rhineland
notes: The Ruhr road back; SOC 2 Uedem 'MANDRIL'.

corridors.name: The Weser road - Wunstorf to Hehlingen
notes: Hannover's fields east over the Leine VOR, Braunschweig (outside the ADIZ by the 1958 exception) to the Hehlingen VOR at Wolfsburg - the I BR Corps sector, the HAWK of 3 and 5 GGW (Aerzen, Velmerstot, Stolzenau) behind.
corridors.src: dewiki ADIZ (Braunschweig); nl.wikipedia Groepen Geleide Wapens

corridors.name: Recovery via the Leine
notes: Hehlingen back over the Leine VOR to Wunstorf; CRC Visselhövede 'SILVERCORK'.

corridors.name: The Heath road south - Fassberg to Hehlingen
notes: Fassberg and Celle south over the Celle NDB to the Hehlingen VOR at Wolfsburg - round the Bergen-Hohne and Munster ranges (ED-R 31/32), into the I BR Corps sector.

corridors.name: Recovery via Celle
notes: Hehlingen back over the Celle NDB to Fassberg; RP Uelzen 'UNITY' and CRC Visselhövede 'SILVERCORK' watching.

corridors.name: The Heath road north - Fassberg to Uelzen
notes: Fassberg north over the Lüneburg Heath to the reporting post at Uelzen ('UNITY'), the I GE Corps sector; Celle joins at the Fassberg NDB.
corridors.src: relikte.com nds_radar; coldwardecoded I NL Corps

corridors.name: Recovery via Fassberg
notes: Uelzen back to Fassberg.

corridors.name: The Elbe road - Hamburg to Lauenburg
notes: Hamburg's fields south-east down the Elbe to Lauenburg, where the border leaves the river - I NL Corps 'just south of Hamburg'.
corridors.src: coldwardecoded I NL Corps; en.wikipedia Inner German border

corridors.name: Recovery up the Elbe
notes: Lauenburg back up the Elbe to Hamburg; CRC Brekendorf 'BUGLE', SOC 1 Brockzetel 'FLYFISH'.

corridors.name: The Trave road - Lübeck to Lauenburg
notes: Lübeck and Kiel south to Lauenburg; the Priwall border and the Lübeck bay Sperrgebiet to the east.

corridors.name: The A2 - Porta to Helmstedt
notes: The Minden Gap to the Helmstedt gate along the Hannover-Berlin autobahn: the center Berlin corridor's own axis, 'the shortest of the three'. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor

corridors.name: The Wendland - Uelzen to Dömitz
notes: Uelzen to the Elbe bridge at Dömitz - the I GE Corps front, across the river into Mecklenburg. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.

corridors.name: Hehlingen to Helmstedt
notes: The last 15 nm from the Hehlingen VOR to the gate - through the front row of the HAWK belt at low level. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.

corridors.name: Lauenburg to Boizenburg
notes: Down the Elbe from Lauenburg to the Boizenburg crossing - the north Berlin corridor's crossing of the border. Curated Low Level Transit Route: 'a temporary corridor of defined dimensions which allows the low-level passage of friendly aircraft through friendly air defenses' (FM 100-103, 1987). The trace is ours.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor

corridors.name: The north corridor axis - Boizenburg to Berlin
notes: The Hamburg-Berlin corridor's centerline: 20 English miles wide, 10,000 ft. Below it the Wittstock 'polygon' and the 41. FRBr ring (Fehrbellin, Beetz, Schönermark).
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor; de.wikipedia Flugabwehrraketentruppen (NVA)

corridors.name: The center corridor axis - Helmstedt to Berlin
notes: The Bückeburg/Hannover-Berlin corridor's centerline over Magdeburg and Genthin; Stendal-Borstel's 135 helicopters north of it, the 41. FRBr's Zachow site at the Berlin end.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor

corridors.name: The south corridor axis - Herleshausen to Berlin
notes: The Frankfurt-Berlin corridor's centerline: over the Thuringian basin, Kelbra, north of Halle and Dessau to the Control Zone - the 51. FRBr (Sprötau) and the 41. FRBr (Markgrafpieske) either side.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor; nva-flieger.de Grenzsperrstreifen

corridors.name: Berlin west - Nauen to Rathenow
notes: The Berlin fields join at Nauen (örtliche Fluglinie 136), clear of the Control Zone, and run west to Rathenow (Zone 064) - the center corridor's axis in reverse.

corridors.name: Recovery via Nauen
notes: Rathenow back over Nauen into the Berlin ring; Bunker Fuchsbau (Fürstenwalde) has the picture.

corridors.name: Berlin north-west - Neuruppin to Pritzwalk
notes: North-west over Neuruppin (730 APIB) to Pritzwalk, the Wittstock routes' first turn (Fluglinie 123).

corridors.name: Recovery via Neuruppin
notes: Pritzwalk back over Neuruppin.

corridors.name: Berlin south-west - Sperenberg to Dessau
notes: South-west over Sperenberg (226 OSAP) and Jüterbog to Dessau - the south corridor's axis in reverse.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor

corridors.name: Recovery via Sperenberg
notes: Dessau back over Sperenberg into the ring.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor

corridors.name: Merseburg - the Harz foot to Kelbra
notes: The southern fields (6 GvIAD Merseburg) west to Kelbra on the Grenzsperrstreifen chain (Fluglinie 177).

corridors.name: Recovery via Kelbra
notes: Kelbra back to Merseburg.

corridors.name: Merseburg north - Cochstedt to Gröningen
notes: North-west over Cochstedt to Gröningen on the chain - the road to the Helmstedt gate.

corridors.name: Recovery via Cochstedt
notes: Gröningen back over Cochstedt.

corridors.name: Parchim - Neustadt-Glewe to Ludwigslust
notes: The Mecklenburg fields south-west over Neustadt-Glewe (Fluglinie 124) to Ludwigslust on the chain - the Elbe crossings beyond.

corridors.name: Recovery via Neustadt-Glewe
notes: Ludwigslust back over Neustadt-Glewe to Parchim.

corridors.name: Parchim south - Perleberg to Osterburg
notes: South over Perleberg and Osterburg (Fluglinie 126) on the chain - the road to the Altmark and Helmstedt.

corridors.name: Recovery via Perleberg
notes: Osterburg back over Perleberg.

corridors.name: Ludwigslust to Boizenburg
notes: The last leg to the Boizenburg crossing - under the HAWK belt's front row beyond the river (FlaRakBtl 37 Belum-Nindorf-Krempel-Gudendorf to the north-west).

corridors.name: Ludwigslust to Dömitz
notes: Ludwigslust to the Dömitz bridge.

corridors.name: Pritzwalk to Boizenburg
notes: The north corridor's axis west: Pritzwalk, Ludwigslust, the Boizenburg crossing.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor

corridors.name: Rathenow to Helmstedt
notes: The center corridor's axis west: Genthin, Magdeburg, the Marienborn crossing at Helmstedt.
corridors.src: FRUS 1945 vol. III doc. 1206 (the corridors, 20 English miles wide); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; en.wikipedia West Berlin Air Corridor

corridors.name: Osterburg to Helmstedt
notes: Down the Altmark over Haldensleben to the Helmstedt gate.

corridors.name: Gröningen to Helmstedt
notes: Gröningen north to the Helmstedt gate.

corridors.name: Kelbra to Herleshausen
notes: Kelbra, Bad Langensalza (Fluglinie 178) and the Werra crossing at Herleshausen - the south corridor's axis west.

corridors.name: Kelbra to Point Alpha
notes: Kelbra south-west over Suhl and Barchfeld on the chain to the Fulda Gap.

corridors.name: Dessau to Herleshausen
notes: Berlin's road west: the south corridor's axis over Halle and Kelbra to the Werra.

text.md_line: **{summary}** — {sector}, {mode} road. Gate **{gate_in}** (WP1), exit at **{gate_out}**. The flight plan is threaded through the structure of 1985 - the ADIZ, the HAWK and Nike belts, the Berlin corridors, the GDR's own flight lines; nobody goes direct across the border.

text.brief_title: CENTRAL REGION CORRIDORS - HOW YOU GET TO THE FIGHT
brief_intro: The flight plan is threaded through the Central Region of 1985: the ADIZ 40 km
west of the border (flight plan and ATC mandatory, USAFE clearance), the HAWK belt
in front of the Nike Hercules belt 150 km back, the three 20-mile Berlin corridors,
the GDR's flight-restriction line and its 'örtliche Fluglinien'. The Low Level
Transit Routes through the belt were never published - 'activated for specified
times only and changed frequently' - so the crossing gates are ours, on the
checkpoints and river crossings the corps sectors used. SOC 1 Brockzetel FLYFISH,
SOC 2 Uedem MANDRIL, SOC 3 Kindsbach; CRC Erndtebrück LONESHIP, Börfink SCANDALISE.
East of the line: Bunker Fuchsbau (Fürstenwalde) and the 41. FRBr ring round Berlin.
brief_sources: Sources: FM 100-103 (1987) Ch. 2; dewiki ADIZ / DHV-Info 49 (1989); relikte.com
(Nike, HAWK, SOC/CRC); nl.wikipedia Groepen Geleide Wapens; A&SF Jul 1983; FRUS 1945
III/1206 (Berlin corridors); nva-flieger.de Luftraum der DDR; de.wikipedia FlaRak-
truppen (NVA), TrÜbPl Wittstock/Altmark/Lieberose; AIP Germany ENR 5.1 (03/24);
known_issues: DCS draws no ADIZ, no belts and no Berlin corridors; the bands, the corridors and the gates on the F10 map are ours, from the published structure. The AI controllers know nothing of FLYFISH, MANDRIL or the BASC; the Nike and HAWK belts are not in the mission unless you place them.
text.sources_line: FM 100-103 · dewiki ADIZ · relikte.com · nl.wikipedia GGW · FRUS 1945 III/1206 · nva-flieger.de · de.wikipedia FlaRak (NVA) / TrÜbPl · AIP Germany ENR 5.1 · NfL 2025-1-3686 · OurAirports · GlobalSecurity
legend: Bands: amber = the ADIZ (40 km); magenta fill = the HAWK belt (LOMEZ); thin magenta = the Nike Hercules belt and the 41. FRBr ring. Thin dashed blue = a 250-ft Low Flying Area, the Berlin Control Zone. Navy hatched = a range (ED-R, or a Soviet Truppenübungsplatz, ~). Dashed amber line = the GDR flight-restriction line.

Gate ring = a crossing point on the inner-German border (all curated, ~). Fix triangle = a navaid or a GDR reference town (~ = placed on the town). The three wide blue lanes are the Berlin air corridors, 20 English miles wide and 10,000 ft - the roads to Berlin. The border, the Elbe and the autobahns are schematic.
